messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty pager fired: private-controlplane-heartbeat-surge for customer "BrightSky Inc." — 5 agents missing heartbeats. Priority: P1. Link: https://pagerduty.example/INC-3091

pagerduty-bot: Incident #INC-3091 auto-created and routed to on-call: elena.

elena: ack — I'm on it.

sam: copying in a handoff window in 10m if needed. tagging tegan for potential escalation.

elena: quick triage: control-plane metrics show heartbeat_rx drop across eu-west-1. hitting agent-management API now.

elena: curl -s -X GET "https://private-controlplane.internal/api/v1/agents?org=brightsky" -H "Authorization: Bearer ***" | jq '.[] | select(.last_heartbeat < (now-120))'

elena: found 5 agents with last_heartbeat ~180-320s ago, all on subnet 10.200.0.0/24.

tegan: any infra/network changes around that time?

sam: yes — infra pushed a route policy update ~17m ago to trim some transit egresss. rolling back now to test.

sam: rollback command:
```
terraform apply -target=module.vpc_peering.route_policy -var='env=prod' -refresh=false
```

elena: attempting immediate fix — sent SSM restart to affected on-prem agents.

elena: SSM command: 
```
sudo systemctl restart redwood-onprem-agent
sudo journalctl -u redwood-onprem-agent -n 200 --no-pager
```

incident-bot: Page update: elena acknowledged at 3017012350. sam escalated to tegan at 3017012400.

tegan: I can take over if rollback doesn't clear in 5m. also preparing a temporary relay fallback to accept heartbeats via regional relay.

elena: after restart, 3/5 agents returned heartbeats. two remain silent. logs show TLS handshake timeout to control-plane.svc:443.

elena: test from host: 
```
curl -v https://controlplane.internal/health -H 'Host: control-plane.svc'
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* timeout after 10s
curl: (28) Operation timed out after 10000 milliseconds
```

sam: rollback applied, BGP converged, traceroute shows path through transit-proxy now. TLS timeouts persisting for two hosts — suspect local egress firewall blocking 443 to CP IP.

tegan: can we push a temporary iptables accept rule to the two hosts?

elena: pushing iptables: 
```
iptables -I OUTPUT -p tcp -d 52.34.120.88 --dport 443 -j ACCEPT
```
(note: control-plane IP resolved during triage: 52.34.120.88)

elena: applied, both agents show heartbeats now, delta normalizing.

elena: customer impact: BrightSky experienced elevated errors for ~14m. API error rate peaked at 6.8%, increased latency and some 502s observed. No data loss. Impact was limited to on-prem agent -> control-plane connectivity causing routing to fall back to degraded paths.

tegan: good mitigation. next steps: full RCA and postmortem. include route_policy change + lack of egress preflight. add runbook step for agent TLS handshake monitoring and an automated egress test.

sam: tagging infra: @infra please review route_policy deploy gating. also @pagerduty keep incident open until RCA + runbook done.

elena: handing off to tegan for post-incident follow-up and customer comms. I'll step out of oncall for 30m (quick break) but reachable.

tegan: taking ownership. I'll draft a customer status update and coordinate RCA. thanks for the fast restart + iptables workaround. :thumbsup: 

pagerduty-bot: Incident #INC-3091 status update: Mitigated -> acknowledged by tegan. Severity P1 -> mitigation in progress. Will post postmortem link here when available.

sam: follow-up item: implement periodic egress healthcheck from on-prem agents to control-plane IPs every 60s and surface failures in Console/Optimize.

elena: added to Optimize backlog, PR planned this week.

tegan: leaving a short summary in the incident tracker and taking ownership for RCA & customer comms. handing off to oncall-sre rotation.
